source_record.description:
Über uns

Wir sind ein Startup aus Hannover und entwickeln eine KI-gestützte Computer-Vision-Plattform für die industrielle Qualitätsprüfung. Unsere Full-Stack-Anwendungen laufen produktiv bei Industriekunden und decken alles ab, von Datenmanagement und Annotation bis zu Modelltraining und Deployment. Dich erwartet ein Engineering-Team von rund 20 Personen mit modernen Arbeitsstrukturen und kurzen Entscheidungswegen.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Verantwortung und Weiterentwicklung unserer Backend-Services: REST-APIs, SQL, Datenbankmigrationen
  • Konzeption und Betreuung unseres Identity and Access Managements (SSO, Rollen, Berechtigungen)
  • Gestaltung unserer Cloud-Architektur: Kubernetes, containerisierte Deployments, S3-kompatibler Object Storage, CI/CD-Pipelines
  • Verantwortung für unsere Produktivsysteme: Monitoring (OTel), Incident Response und der zuverlässige Betrieb kritischer Infrastruktur bei unseren Kunden
  • Code-Reviews, Arbeit im Team und aktive Mitgestaltung unseres agilen Entwicklungsprozesses von der Planung bis zum Release

Dein Profil

  • Mindestens 4 Jahre Berufserfahrung in der Softwareentwicklung mit fundierter Expertise in Backend und Datenbanken
  • Praktische Erfahrung im Betrieb von Produktivsystemen: Kubernetes, Docker, CI/CD, Infrastructure as Code, On-Premise und Cloud
  • Erfahrung in agiler Zusammenarbeit und im Umgang mit Tools wie Linear, Jira oder vergleichbaren Lösungen
  • Sicherheit über den gesamten Stack: Du debuggst APIs, prüfst Infrastrukturänderungen und diskutierst Architekturentscheidungen
  • Pragmatische und selbstständige Arbeitsweise und Eigenverantwortung
  • Fließende Deutschkenntnisse und gute Englischkenntnisse im beruflichen Alltag

Wünschenswert

  • Erfahrung mit Computer Vision, ML-Plattformen, Distributed Computing oder datenintensiven Systemen
  • Erfahrung mit Identity Providern und API-Sicherheit

Wir bieten

  • Eine moderne Engineering-Kultur: Code-Reviews, CI/CD, agile Arbeitsweise und aktuelles Tooling
  • Eine ausgereifte Produktivinfrastruktur im Einsatz bei Industriekunden
  • Mit unserem Wachstum wächst auch die technische Bandbreite: Du lernst neue Bereiche kennen, statt auf ein Thema festgelegt zu sein
  • Flache Hierarchien und direkten Einfluss auf Entscheidungen
  • Ein wertschätzendes Miteinander in einem kollegialen Team, in dem man sich gegenseitig unterstützt und auch mal gemeinsam Zeit verbringt
  • Flexibles, hybrides Arbeiten in einem wachsenden Team in Hannover

  • Pathfinder Fellowship: Helping grow the global network of AI safety university groups from a few dozen to nearly 100, with $9.5M in funding over the next two years to support their work.

We see ourselves as a portfolio of highly impactful projects in a fast-evolving field. Over the next six months, we expect to double in size and launch several new initiatives addressing critical gaps in the ecosystem.

 

The Role

University groups are where many people first get involved in AI safety, and Kairos provides most of the support these groups get today. Through the Pathfinder Fellowship, we provide mentorship and funding to organizers of AI safety university groups around the world, and through OASIS we bring top organizers together for in-person workshops. Over the past year, this work has grown from a fraction of our time to one of our core priorities, and we’re now building a team around it.

We’re looking for a Head of Groups to own this area as a whole and make it more ambitious. You’d set the strategy for how we plan to support AI safety university groups, decide which new initiatives we pursue, and build the team behind them. You would report to Neav Topaz (co-director).

It’d be up to you what the groups team pursues, but we’re weighing several ambitious directions, like hiring full-time organizers in key regions, running residencies for top organizers, seeding new groups at strong universities we’re not yet reaching, and giving the strongest groups much more hands-on support.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Set the strategy for how we support university groups. You’ll decide where the work goes next, how our programs fit together, and what we should start, stop, or scale.

  • Launch new initiatives. You’ll choose which new directions we pursue, like regional organizers, residencies, and focused support for top universities, and get them up and running.

  • Own how we support and fund groups. You’ll set the bar for which groups and organizers we invest in, and decide where our funding goes.

  • Strong judgment about people. Much of the job is deciding which organizers to back and who to hire, often with limited evidence.

  • Ambitious and high agency. You’re excited to push this work well past its current size and quality bar. You’ll own the portfolio from day one, and should be comfortable building a vision, executing on it autonomously, and answering big open questions as they come up.

  • Mission-aligned. You care deeply about the risks from advanced AI, and you think university groups are one of the most promising ways to help reduce them.

  • You’ll be working toward reducing risks from advanced AI, potentially the most important challenge of our time. The groups you support are where many future AI safety and policy professionals get their start.

  • University groups are a central part of Kairos’s strategy over the coming years, and you’d own how we scale that work.

  • Salary: $140,000–$195,000 (baseline), $175,000–$245,000 (supported hubs, like London, DC, Boston, and NYC), or $195,000–$270,000 (San Francisco Bay Area), depending on experience, with potential for additional compensation for exceptional candidates

  • Location: This is a remote role. We provide access to office space in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston, with optional coworking elsewhere. If you work from an AI safety office in one of these cities, we cover food, lunches, and office expenses. If you work from home, we cover home office expenses.

  • Benefits: Flexible working hours, highly competitive health insurance, dental and vision coverage, generous vacation policy, and professional development budget

  • Team retreats: We host all-team retreats three times a year to connect in person, collaborate, and build team culture.

  • Travel: Work-related travel and expenses covered.

 

Logistics

  • Start date: Ideally by October or early November 2026, with flexibility for the right candidate

  • Remote, with expected travel 3–6 times a year for conferences and events, predominantly in the US

  • We’d also be happy for you to work out of any of the AI safety hubs in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston.

  • We prefer candidates who can attend meetings in the ET time zone (though our team currently spans GMT-8 to GMT+1).

  • Kairos is happy to sponsor visas to the US (typically H-1Bs or O-1As) and will likely be able to sponsor UK visas in the coming months. We can’t guarantee visa approvals, however.

 

Our Culture

We’re a small, high-trust team motivated by the urgent challenge of making advanced AI go well. We try hard to figure out where we’re wrong, which means we say uncomfortable things to each other and change our minds fairly often. We value collaborative truth-seeking, a scout mindset, agility, and an alliance mindset with the broader ecosystem.

We also believe meaningful work should be enjoyable. We support each other’s well-being, celebrate wins, and maintain a healthy sense of humor even when the work is hard.

 

Application Process

We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis.

  1. Application form (10–20 mins)

  2. Take-home assignment (2–4 hours, paid)

  3. Interview (45 mins)

  4. Reference checks

  5. Work trial (3 days, paid)

  6. Offer

If you’re excited about this role but unsure whether you meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. If you’re interested in multiple roles, apply to the one that best fits your skills and interests, and note in your application the other roles that you’d like to be considered for.

cards.announcement: The product you will work on The HOLOPLOT Matrix Array is a new type of sound system built around precise, software-defined control of sound in three dimensions - grounded in physics and implemented through a combination of custom hardware and purpose-built software. HOLOPLOT deployed Matrix Arrays in various venues, including the Sphere in Las Vegas - the world’s most advanced entertainment venue and, notably, home to the world’s largest audio installation in entertainment. Audio processing in HOLOPLOT systems is distributed: every loudspeaker runs embedded Linux, and hundreds of them have to be configured, coordinated, monitored, and updated as one system. This is enabled by multiple open source and in-house developed services running on an on-premises Kubernetes cluster. AWS-hosted services connect venues to remote monitoring, telemetry, and configuration. Many venues are air-gapped or only intermittently connected for remote servicing, and that constraint shapes most of the design decisions in the platform. The ideal candidate is We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer who builds the platform our sound systems run on, and who takes responsibility for how it behaves in production. This is a software engineering role first. You will spend your time writing software, either with your own team or embedded with one of the other HOLOPLOT teams: services, controllers, agents, and tooling that provision, configure, observe, and update our systems. Our infrastructure is defined as code and evolves through the same review and release process as the rest of our software. You design the operational side, you build it, and you are on call when it misbehaves in the field. Your role and responsibilities You will join the team that owns the platform underneath our installations and connected services, working alongside backend, embedded, and frontend engineers who are organized in cross-functional product teams. Build the platform Architect and implement services to provision, configure, and manage server fleets across AWS and local clusters. Create control-plane logic for venue systems to ensure consistency, health monitoring, rollout management, and recovery, even during uplink disruptions. Establish end-to-end provisioning workflows for embedded Linux hardware, spanning from initial manufacturing to customer deployment. Enhance update processes to streamline software deployments for active customer installations. Develop APIs and developer tooling that empower engineering teams to independently deploy, observe, and troubleshoot their services. Embed telemetry capabilities into the platform to facilitate remote diagnosis of venue system behavior . Run what you build Own the AWS infrastructure behind our connected services: remote access, access control, telemetry ingestion, remote backup, secret management, and monitoring. All of it is infrastructure as code. Operate and evolve the on-premises Kubernetes footprint at venues, including air-gapped and intermittently connected installations. Monitor large environments, investigate problems across the software/hardware boundary, and turn each incident into a fix in the code. Be part of a compensated on-call rotation Set the technical direction Advise and collaborate with product teams on building distributed systems that are scalable, secure, and observable, and review their designs with production reality in mind. Research and introduce tools and technologies where they measurably improve how we build and operate. Contribute back to the open-source projects we depend on, through issues and fixes. What you need to succeed in this role Several years of professional software engineering experience, most of it spent designing and shipping production systems. The product you will work on

The HOLOPLOT Matrix Array is a new type of sound system built around precise, software-defined control of sound in three dimensions - grounded in physics and implemented through a combination of custom hardware and purpose-built software. HOLOPLOT deployed Matrix Arrays in various venues, including the Sphere in Las Vegas - the world’s most advanced entertainment venue and, notably, home to the world’s largest audio installation in entertainment. 


Audio processing in HOLOPLOT systems is distributed: every loudspeaker runs embedded Linux, and hundreds of them have to be configured, coordinated, monitored, and updated as one system. This is enabled by multiple open source and in-house developed services running on an on-premises Kubernetes cluster. AWS-hosted services connect venues to remote monitoring, telemetry, and configuration. Many venues are air-gapped or only intermittently connected for remote servicing, and that constraint shapes most of the design decisions in the platform.


The ideal candidate is

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer who builds the platform our sound systems run on, and who takes responsibility for how it behaves in production.


This is a software engineering role first. You will spend your time writing software, either with your own team or embedded with one of the other HOLOPLOT teams: services, controllers, agents, and tooling that provision, configure, observe, and update our systems. Our infrastructure is defined as code and evolves through the same review and release process as the rest of our software. You design the operational side, you build it, and you are on call when it misbehaves in the field.


Your role and responsibilities

You will join the team that owns the platform underneath our installations and connected services, working alongside backend, embedded, and frontend engineers who are organized in cross-functional product teams.


Build the platform

  • Architect and implement services to provision, configure, and manage server fleets across AWS and local clusters.

  • Create control-plane logic for venue systems to ensure consistency, health monitoring, rollout management, and recovery, even during uplink disruptions.

  • Establish end-to-end provisioning workflows for embedded Linux hardware, spanning from initial manufacturing to customer deployment.

  • Enhance update processes to streamline software deployments for active customer installations.

  • Develop APIs and developer tooling that empower engineering teams to independently deploy, observe, and troubleshoot their services.

  • Embed telemetry capabilities into the platform to facilitate remote diagnosis of venue system behavior

  • .

Run what you build

  • Own the AWS infrastructure behind our connected services: remote access, access control, telemetry ingestion, remote backup, secret management, and monitoring. All of it is infrastructure as code.

  • Operate and evolve the on-premises Kubernetes footprint at venues, including air-gapped and intermittently connected installations.

  • Monitor large environments, investigate problems across the software/hardware boundary, and turn each incident into a fix in the code.

  • Be part of a compensated on-call rotation


Set the technical direction

  • Advise and collaborate with product teams on building distributed systems that are scalable, secure, and observable, and review their designs with production reality in mind.

  • Research and introduce tools and technologies where they measurably improve how we build and operate.

  • Contribute back to the open-source projects we depend on, through issues and fixes.


What you need to succeed in this role

  • Several years of professional software engineering experience, most of it spent designing and shipping production systems.

  • Fluency in software engineering as a craft: concurrency, error handling, testing, and designing APIs that other teams build on.

  • Working knowledge of the Kubernetes control plane and the operator/controller pattern, including how clusters behave when they are unhealthy.

  • Hands-on experience with AWS, and a firm belief in infrastructure as code. Terraform and Ansible are what we use today.

  • Comfort across several languages, and the ability to pick up a new one when the problem calls for it. Our platform work is mostly Go and Python, with Rust and C++ elsewhere in the stack.

  • Experience building distributed systems, and a clear understanding of how they fail: partitions, partial rollouts, clock skew, retries, and reconciliation.

  • A good sense for software architecture and maintainability, and the habit of writing code that colleagues can pick up and change.

  • A strong command of Linux, scripting, and automation.

  • Experience instrumenting software for telemetry and using it to answer real questions about running systems.

  • Good judgment about what to automate and what to leave alone.

  • Strong communication skills in English. You can explain a design or a failure clearly to engineers, product stakeholders, and non-specialists.

  • Willingness to take part in compensated on-call and weekend work when installations need it.

  • A can-do mentality, an eye for detail, and the courage to take on problems outside your comfort zone.

  • Experience in using AI for engineering.

  • Experience with NATS, Prometheus/Thanos, or PostgreSQL in production.

  • Experience with air-gapped or intermittently connected installations.

  • Experience running Kubernetes in production, not only deploying to it.

  • Experience with embedded Linux, device fleet management, or IoT security.

  • Networking depth: multicast at scale, WireGuard, BGP, IPv6.

  • Experience in the audio, broadcast, or live events industry.

  • Contributions to open-source infrastructure projects

reisetopia ist in den vergangenen Jahren deutlich gewachsen.   • Große Lust, dich schnell und selbstständig in neue Themen einzuarbeiten und stetig dazuzulernen
